description:
Replace an exact unique snippet of text in a Google Doc (like a local file Edit). old_string is matched markup-tolerantly; ambiguous matches return surrounding context to disambiguate; a table is matched as its rows, in the form read_doc shows it (a pipe table, or the HTML of a styled one). Elements read_doc shows are kept when old_string and new_string both hold them as read (a person chip inside a sentence you reword survives), deleted when new_string leaves them out, and created when new_string adds one: [^label] with a [^label]: note line, Nov 15, 2026 (the text’s shape picks the date format), for a person or for a Drive file, with its line, and --- for a rule. A column break, equation, page-number field, or link chip to anything but a Drive file cannot be made: it is refused before anything is sent, and a chip’s text is Google’s (a chip given other words is refused). A footnote’s note is edited by quoting its [^1]: line, and a dropdown’s list by quoting its line. INSERTING IS AN EDIT: quote the text to add after (or before), write it back in new_string, and add the new content to it. Text from old_string that comes back unchanged is kept as it is, with its style, comments and suggestions, so old_string `| Total | $4,200 |` and new_string `| Total | $4,200 | Payment due within 30 days.` leaves the table alone and adds the paragraph after it; a match that ends in a table puts the new blocks after the whole table. An anchor in the middle of a paragraph splits the paragraph there. A new block carries its own style, not its anchor’s: a paragraph added after a heading, a Title or a list item is Normal text with no bullet unless the markdown says otherwise, while text added inside an existing paragraph keeps that paragraph’s style. An empty doc, tab, header or footer has nothing to anchor on: use write_doc. new_string is the same markdown and inline HTML write_doc takes: headings, lists, tables, images (`` or `![alt](src)`; a centered one is `

`, local files resolve against baseDir), page breaks, and inline constructs (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, [text](url), ``, ``, `

`, `

`, and a page break as a line of its own: `

`, so new_string `Title page
` puts what follows on a new page; old_string can span a break) — the same spelling read_doc emits, so a read can be edited and written back. STYLE IS CSS, and this is the only way to change it. Restyle text you are not otherwise changing by giving the same words with different markup: old_string `

4. Term`, new_string `

4. Term` sends only style requests — no delete, no insert, so a long paragraph is never retyped and its words cannot change; markup missing from new_string is cleared (drop the wrapper to remove an indent). To restyle a whole named style, edit its rule in read_doc’s

account.description: Google account email to use. Defaults to GDOCS_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT, or the sole account.

baseDir.description: absolute dir to resolve relative local image paths and contentFile against

confirmLoss.description: the confirmLoss string from the refusal of a table edit that moves a row or column whose text comments quote, passed back exactly, after the user has agreed that those comments are lost. Never needed otherwise.

contentFile.description: path to a local markdown/text file to use as new_string, read directly by the server — preferred for long text. Absolute, or relative to baseDir. Mutually exclusive with new_string.

old_string.description: exact text to replace (quote a unique slice from read_doc)

page.description: which header/footer, when a doc defines more than one (default-page, first-page, even-page). Omit to use whichever exists.

path.description: The doc or tab: a Drive id or URL, /folder/doc, or /folder/doc/tab (nested: /folder/doc/tab/child). A doc with one tab needs no tab step; a doc with several is refused until one is named, and the refusal lists every tab path.

segment.description: which content tree to target: body (default), or the page header/footer. Header/footer content is invisible to a body read — a letterhead logo lives there.

suggest.description: send the edit as suggestions for a person to accept or reject, instead of applying it (default false)

name: edit_doc
title: Edit a Google Doc
